frozenBy: measured from the captures in _captures/ (pixel-level inspection of the originals)

screen.grid: box coordinates are in 0..1000 top-left normalised units: x = pixelX/1920*1000, y = pixelY/1200*1000
screen.notes: Every capture in this set is a real 1920x1200 desktop screenshot. The boxes were measured on the pixels themselves, not estimated: the icon boxes come from an ink/colour segmentation of the original PNG, the button boxes from their drawn borders, the clock and tab label from their glyph runs, the game character from the cyan silhouette cluster, and the cat head from the texture map of the photo. There is no vision-model guess in any of them.

scoring.absentRule: With no refusal option in the model contract, the pet always commits to a place and always draws. An absent target therefore cannot be answered with 'no draw': the honest measurement is WHERE the invented mark landed, so the absent cases are a hallucination probe and not a pass gate. The scorer still counts them, and reports them, but the pass line does not depend on them.
scoring.primaryMetric: point in box for present items; the hallucination landing for absent items
scoring.secondaryMetric: centre distance in normalised units, computed over misses (present items only)

cases.name: desktop recycle bin icon
cases.request: circle the recycle bin icon on my desktop
cases.target: the recycle bin icon in the top-left corner of the desktop
cases.note: The ink of the bin graphic only, measured as the difference from the desktop background colour: x 20..55, y 8..51. The 'Recycle Bin' label below (y 61..72) is NOT part of the box.

cases.name: yellow desktop folder
cases.request: circle the yellow folder on my desktop
cases.target: the yellow folder icon on the desktop (upper of the two folders)
cases.note: The yellow pixels of the folder graphic: x 549..590, y 111..143. Its label sits below and is excluded. A second yellow item exists lower down (y 159..167) and is not the target.

cases.name: taskbar search box
cases.request: circle the search box on my taskbar
cases.target: the search box (the rounded pill) on the taskbar
cases.note: The pill's own rounded rectangle: top edge at y 1160, bottom at y 1191, widest at x 652..873. The magnifier glyph and the placeholder text are inside it.

cases.name: taskbar clock
cases.request: circle the clock on my taskbar
cases.target: the clock (the time and date) at the right of the taskbar
cases.note: The two text lines only: the time at y 1164..1171 and the date at y 1180..1188. The system-tray icons to the left (x 1760..1840) are not part of it.

cases.name: large window on the left
cases.request: circle the big window on the left side of the screen
cases.target: the File Explorer window occupying the left half of the screen
cases.note: The VISIBLE extent of the window: the acrylic title bar starts at y 8, the left border is x 7 (x 4..6 is drop shadow, excluded), the right edge is x 952 where another window overlaps it, and the window runs down to the taskbar at y 1152. A large-object case: the point-in-box metric only needs the centre inside this rectangle.

cases.name: game character
cases.request: circle the cyan character on my screen
cases.target: the cyan humanoid character silhouette on the right of the game screen
cases.note: The larger of the two cyan clusters in the frame (the other is a small one at x 1640..1659, y 599..637). Measured by hue and saturation, so the box is the silhouette itself and not a HUD element.

cases.name: cat head in a photo
cases.target: the cat's head in the photo on the right of the screen
cases.note: Ear tips at (1138, 435) and (1339, 428); the head runs down to the chin where it merges into the chest fur near y 550. The same pixels are visible in _captures/c-edgecat.png, where the photo is not covered by another window.

cases.name: terminal tab label
cases.target: the text 'oceanic-unified' in the tab strip
cases.note: The glyph run of the label itself (x 1403..1484, y 51..60). The small icon to its left (x 1385..1394) and the second copy of the same name lower down (about x 1100..1160, y 84..97) are excluded.

cases.name: Save button
cases.note: The whole button face including its small disk icon: the drawn border runs x 911..994, y 706..728. The 'Save' word itself is x 967..990.

cases.name: Cancel button (distractor next to Save)
cases.target: the button labelled 'Cancel', the distractor next to Save
cases.note: The second button of the same action row, 16 px to the right of Save: the drawn border runs x 1011..1094, y 706..728. Both G09 and G10 are in one screenshot on purpose, so the two labels are distractors for each other.

cases.name: absent elephant
cases.target: the elephant (which is NOT on this screen)
cases.note: A hallucination probe, not a pass gate: the model is never offered a refusal, so it commits to a place and draws. What is measured is WHERE the invented mark landed. The desktop is busy enough that there are tempting false anchors.

cases.name: absent printer icon
cases.target: the printer icon (which is NOT on this screen)
cases.note: The same probe against a game frame rather than a desktop, so the background type does not confound it.

cases.name: Valorant shortcut icon
cases.request: circle the small red Valorant icon on my desktop
cases.target: the small red VALORANT shortcut icon (the red V in a square frame) in the lower left of the desktop
cases.note: Added on November 9, 2026 for the detector-first phase, and measured on the pixels: the red border of the Riot shortcut square runs x 92..135, y 989..1032 (44 by 44 pixels). The 'VALORANT' word under it (y 1041+) is NOT part of the box. The desktop also holds a yellow folder shortcut labelled 'VALORANT...' lower down and to the right; that one is not the target, and the request says 'small red' so the two cannot be confused.
